exercise: Junior AI Engineer take-home, Alternative E: Incident-to-patch (starter pack 2026-10-02)

development_tools_and_models.notes: Claude Code VS Code extension (anthropic.claude-code 2.1.289 at the start, auto-updated to 2.1.292 during the exercise) in VS Code 1.138.0 on Linux. Development model: Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5) at effort 'high', set by the user-level modelSettings (global default 'xhigh' for other models). Same session throughout, no model switches.

plugins_and_extensions.notes: Only the Claude Code extension itself. No marketplace plugins were installed or enabled; the built-in plugins that ship with Claude Code were left at their defaults. The IDE integration attached VS Code diagnostics after edits automatically (built-in, not configured).

application_models_and_parameters.notes: Anthropic Python SDK anthropic==1.11.0. Model claude-opus-5-5; output_config.effort 'medium'; adaptive thinking (model default, cannot be disabled); max_tokens 16000; structured output via output_config.format json_schema (PROPOSAL_SCHEMA in assistant/model.py); server-side refusal fallback (beta server-side-fallback-2026-07-01, fallbacks='default'); API timeout 300 s; SDK default 2 retries. Temperature not set (not supported on this model). Overridable via INCIDENT_MODEL, INCIDENT_EFFORT, INCIDENT_FALLBACKS or --model/--effort.

skills.notes: claude-api (bundled with Claude Code, invoked once on 2026-10-06) was used as an SDK reference before writing assistant/model.py: current model ID, structured outputs, typed error classes, fallbacks. It is part of the Claude Code install, so it is not-exportable as a file. The starter pack's generate-assignment-data skill was read (SKILL.md) but not installed or invoked; fixtures were handwritten following its guidance. No custom skills were created.

agent_instructions_and_subagents.notes: Project instructions in CLAUDE.md (frozen-fixture rules, answer-key rule, conventions). Two auto-memory files written during the exercise; sanitized copies saved. No subagents were defined or spawned.

hooks_and_scripts.notes: Git pre-commit hooks (not Claude Code hooks): ruff, ruff-format, pydoclint, pre-commit-hooks, an Anthropic-key scanner, the frozen-hash check, the reference verification and pytest. They run on `git commit` only after `pre-commit install`; read .pre-commit-config.yaml before enabling. Claude Code hooks (settings.json 'hooks'): not-used.

prompts_and_rules.notes: prompts/system.md is the application's system prompt (unchanged since commit cde3b1e). The user message is assembled in assistant/model.py:build_request and saved verbatim per run as runs/<id>/model/request.json. pyproject.toml holds the lint and docstring rules the code must follow.

tool_and_mcp_settings.notes: No MCP servers configured (no .mcp.json; mcpServers empty in ~/.claude.json). A claude.ai document connector was available in the session but not used. The application gives the model no tools: it returns one structured JSON proposal.

permissions_and_environment_names.notes: Default Claude Code permission mode; every command was approved or denied interactively. No allowlist, no project .claude/settings.json or settings.local.json. Two calls were denied by the user and adapted to (a commit carrying an AI attribution trailer, a headless Firefox screenshot). Environment variable names are in .env.example; the real key lives in the git-ignored .env.
